description: The Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project is the largest long-running collection of hospital discharge records in the United States, covering who is admitted, why, for how long, at what charge and whether they come back. It is run by the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality in partnership with state data organisations. The National Inpatient Sample holds about 7 million stays a year, a 20 percent stratified sample of community hospital discharges that weights up to over 33 million hospitalisations, with years from 1988 to 2023, and sister databases cover children, emergency department visits, readmissions, ambulatory surgery and full state files. Each record carries diagnosis and procedure codes, demographics, hospital characteristics, payer, total charges and severity measures. The microdata are available only as a paid download through the HCUP Central Distributor after online training and a data use agreement, with prices set by the data organisations, while the HCUPnet query tool gives free aggregate statistics online. Caveats: records count stays, not people in most files, redistribution is prohibited, and some states restrict elements. Simulation uses: calibrating hospital and emergency department demand, length-of-stay and readmission rates in capacity and surge models. Related records: the CMS hospital cost reports (data-cms-hcris-cost-reports) give the matching supply and finance side.
licence: HCUP Data Use Agreement (proprietary; no redistribution)
name: AHRQ Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project (HCUP): US inpatient, emergency department and ambulatory surgery databases (NIS, KID, NEDS, NRD, SID, SEDD) and HCUPnet
provider: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ), US Department of Health and Human Services, with state data organisations
schema_summary: Discharge-level records: ICD-10-CM/PCS diagnosis, procedure and external-cause codes, patient demographics, hospital characteristics, expected payment source, total charges, severity and comorbidity measures; nationwide samples (NIS about 7 million stays a year, a 20 percent stratified sample of community hospital discharges since 2012; KID paediatric; NEDS emergency visits; NRD readmissions; NASS ambulatory surgery) and state databases (SID, SASD, SEDD)

sources.note: HCUP databases page: nationwide NIS, KID, NASS, NEDS, NRD and state SID, SASD, SEDD; enable users to 'identify, track, and analyze national trends in healthcare utilization, access, charges, quality, and outcomes'

NIS overview: data available from 1988 through 2023; approximately 7 million unweighted stays a year, estimating over 33 million hospitalizations; since 2012 a 20-percent stratified sample of all discharges from US community hospitals; ICD-10-CM/PCS codes, demographics, hospital characteristics, payment source, total charges, severity and comorbidity measures; purchased through CDORS after the online Data Use Agreement training

Purchase through the HCUP Central Distributor Online Reporting System after training and signing the Data Use Agreement; 'Participating data organizations set the price of their data'; reduced pricing for some grantees, students and non-profits
HCUPnet: free online tool giving inpatient, emergency department and community (patient county) statistics from NIS, KID, NEDS, NRD and SID, 2011 onward to 2023

spatial_resolution: Discharge records with hospital and state identifiers; HCUPnet by nation, state and patient county
